definitions.explanation: A deep, vivid blue color traditionally derived from the mineral lapis lazuli. Widely used in Japanese art, particularly in nihonga (Japanese-style painting). Also used more broadly to describe a rich, deep blue in everyday language.

examples.japanese: {群青|ぐんじょう}{色|いろ}の{空|そら}が{広|ひろ}がっていた。
examples.english: A deep blue sky stretched out above.

examples.japanese: {夕暮|ゆうぐ}れの{海|うみ}が{群青|ぐんじょう}に{染|そ}まっていく。
examples.english: The sea at dusk is being dyed in ultramarine blue.

examples.japanese: この{日本画|にほんが}には{群青|ぐんじょう}と{金箔|きんぱく}がふんだんに{使|つか}われており、{豪華|ごうか}な{印象|いんしょう}を{与|あた}える。
examples.english: This Japanese-style painting uses ultramarine blue and gold leaf abundantly, giving a luxurious impression.

notes:
USAGE:
Often used in compound form {群青|ぐんじょう}{色|いろ} to explicitly mean "ultramarine color." A culturally significant pigment in traditional Japanese painting ({日本画|にほんが}), where it is one of the most prized mineral pigments. Also commonly encountered as an evocative color word in literature and song lyrics.

NOTE:
The Yoasobi song "{群青|ぐんじょう}" (2020) made this word widely known among younger generations.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {群青|ぐんじょう}{色|いろ}: ultramarine blue (as a color name)
- {群青|ぐんじょう}の{空|そら}: deep blue sky
- {群青|ぐんじょう}の{海|うみ}: deep blue sea
